app.name: Home Tutor
welcome.tagline: Free home learning for children aged 3 to 17. Learn real skills, at your own pace, with your family, tutor or class.
welcome.free.title: Free for everyone
welcome.free.body: No ads, no fees and no expensive equipment. Every activity has an almost-free version.
welcome.offline.title: Works offline
welcome.offline.body: Lessons, quizzes and progress work without internet and sync when it comes back.
welcome.private.title: Private by design
welcome.private.body: No trackers. You decide what is saved, and you can export or delete it at any time.
picker.title: Who is learning today?
picker.empty: Add your first child to begin.
setup.title: Set up your family
setup.step0.intro: Hello! I am Sprout. Let's set up Home Tutor for your family. It takes two minutes.
setup.step1.intro: How will you use Home Tutor? You can change this later.
setup.step2.intro: Choose a parent PIN. It keeps the parent and tutor areas just for grown-ups.
setup.step3.intro: Last step: your consent for your child's profile.
setup.mode.healthNote: The health and growing-up lessons stay switched off until you turn them on in each child's profile.
setup.pin.why: Children can use the app freely. The PIN protects settings, health options and data controls.
setup.pin.invalid: The PIN must be 4 to 6 numbers.
setup.pin.mismatch: The two PINs are different. Please try again.
setup.consent.title: Your consent
setup.consent.p1: I am the parent or legal guardian (or I have their permission) and I create the child profiles.
setup.consent.p2: Children never get their own email or account. Only a first name or nickname and birth year and month are needed.
setup.consent.p3: Everything stays on this device unless I choose to sign in to save progress in the cloud.
setup.consent.p4: Home Tutor teaches. It does not diagnose, and it does not replace doctors, instructors or professionals.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.updated: Plain-English privacy notice. Last updated 25 November 2026.
privacy.short.title: The short version
privacy.short.body: Home Tutor has no ads, no trackers and no third-party analytics. It works without an account. If you create one, we keep only what is needed to save your family's learning, and you can export or delete it at any time.
privacy.collect.title: What we keep
privacy.collect.body: On your device: family name, the parent PIN (as a hash), child profiles (first name or nickname, birth year and month, country, languages, interests, goals, settings) and learning progress. In the cloud, only if you sign in: the same data, plus a hash of your email and a slow salted hash of your password.
privacy.notCollect.title: What we never collect
privacy.notCollect.body: No photos, no precise location, no contacts, no surnames, no school names, no advertising IDs and no tracking cookies. Children never have their own accounts or email addresses.
privacy.device.title: Data on your device
privacy.device.body: Without an account everything stays in this browser or app. Clearing the app's data or using Delete all data removes it.
privacy.cloud.title: Data in the cloud
privacy.cloud.body: With an account, data is stored on Cloudflare (Workers and D1) so it can sync between your devices. It is used only to run Home Tutor, never sold and never shared.
privacy.children.title: Children's privacy (COPPA and GDPR-K)
privacy.children.body: The parent or guardian creates every child profile and gives consent at set-up. We ask for the minimum: a first name or nickname and birth year and month. Health modules are off until the parent switches them on.
privacy.key.title: Progress Keys
privacy.key.body: A Progress Key shows a read-only passport (first name, age, skills and progress) to whoever has the code. You choose the expiry and can revoke it at any time. The code is stored only as a hash.
privacy.rights.title: Your rights
privacy.rights.body: You can see, correct, export and delete all data at any time from the app: Family settings for this device, Account and sync for the cloud. Deleting the account removes all cloud data straight away.
privacy.security.title: Security
privacy.security.body: Passwords are hashed with PBKDF2 and a random salt in the server. Sign-in attempts are rate limited. Sessions use random tokens stored as hashes. All traffic uses HTTPS.
privacy.laws.title: Laws we design for
privacy.laws.body: We follow data-minimisation principles from COPPA (USA), GDPR and the UK Age Appropriate Design Code, and India's DPDP Act. This notice is not legal advice; it will be reviewed before wider release.
privacy.contact.title: Questions
privacy.contact.body: Questions, ideas or a privacy request? Open an issue on the project's public GitHub Issues page. It is public, so please never post your email, your children's names or any other personal details there. To delete your data, the quickest way is Delete my account in the app.
about.title: About Home Tutor
about.mascot: Meet Sprout, our helper. Like every child, Sprout grows a little every day.
about.body1: Home Tutor is a free learning companion for parents, tutors and teachers with one child, siblings, a small group or a whole class, for ages 3 to 17.
about.body2: It combines core subjects with life skills, physical education, first aid, nature, money, technology, languages, arts, philosophy, careers and real projects, and asks one question: what does this child need next?
about.safety.title: The safety engine
about.safety.body: Every practical activity carries one of these ratings, plus a Basic (almost free), Better (low cost) and Advanced version, and ideas for what to use if you do not have the equipment.
about.medical.title: Medical and professional boundary
about.medical.body: Home Tutor is an educational app. It does not diagnose and does not replace doctors, nurses, physiotherapists, psychologists, certified first-aid instructors, qualified sports instructors or professional tradespeople. Where a skill needs certification, the lesson says so and points to an accredited local course.
about.credits.title: Pictures and sources
about.credits.body: All pictures are original drawings made in code and standard emoji. No AI-generated images are used. Lessons cite public sources such as WHO, UNESCO, UNICEF, NHS, the Red Cross and Red Crescent, and national safety bodies. Read-aloud uses your device's own voice.
about.rights: © Home Tutor. All rights reserved until the owner chooses a licence.
credits.title: Photo and book credits
credits.intro: Every photo here is openly licensed or in the public domain. We keep a copy on our own server, so your device never contacts other websites to show it. Tap a photo to see who took it.
credits.books: Books you can read free online
